Canonical design: `docs/DESIGN.md` (exported from the original Claude design doc; edit it here from now on).
Standing instructions for Claude sessions: `CLAUDE.md`. Owner's VPS guide: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.

- Owner directive 2026-10-19 (more demo learning trades): `box_break_close` also runs on 30m (shadow roster amendment
  2026-10-19b, docs/research/shadow-roster-2026-10-19.md; roster 4 of 40, K +1). 30m is a known timeframe end to end
  (`TF_SECONDS`, store table `bars_30m`, release resample `HIGHER_TFS`, scripts/build_bars.py); time exit 72 bars
  (36 h). Not 5m: the engine's base clock is 15m, so a 5m agent would decide one bar in three; it needs a 5m base clock
  first (engine/exit-path lane, trading-safety). No money-flow rule agent exists to extend. Deploy: re-sync release bars
  on the brain so `bars_30m` exists (the replica bootstrap reads it); the engine service creates the 30m RuleModel
  challenger itself at load (`ensure_rule_challenger`).
- `box_break_close` (owner's box strategy) runs in the engine as SHADOW rule agents on 15m, 1h and 4h: a close through a replica box by 20% of its height, mfi out of 30/70 and turning, not against the swing trend, not in the golden zone; stop 1.5 ATR (beyond the box), target 2R. The shadow-host engine now attaches `ReplicaShadow` (state in aux.db, bootstrapped from the store's bars since `tv.replica_series_start` 2016-01-01; short 4h tails extended from the store). Each roster agent gets a `RuleModel` challenger (p = "fired", uncalibrated; ADR 0038); an uncalibrated model never sizes a live entry. Roster frozen in docs/research/shadow-roster-2026-10-19.md (3 agents; the other research families are listed with what blocks them). Bootstraps run on a background thread (bounded to the last 2 full years); demo cost probes may mirror roster rule agents (trading-safety ruling 2026-10-19).

Records only in aux.db `cost_probes` (migration 14) via `goldbot/engine/cost_probe.py` (`probes()` is the costs-v2 reader); never in closed_trades.jsonl, the store's fills, the phase gate, the throttle, attribution or the shadow scoring. The broker ledger reconciles closed probes against `cost_probes`. `cost_probe: {enabled: true}` in config/accounts.yaml is refused on any non-demo account at load and at engine start. Trading-safety round 1: probes carry their own magic (base + 97) and a `cp-` comment, so a probe found without its order row is adopted as `cost_probe:orphan` (`cost_probe.adoption`, which replaced `Engine._agent_for_magic`), never as a live trade; a probe budget (`budget_share` 0.2 of the day's loss allowance) stops new probes; making way skips a close already due; an unconfirmed-send probe keeps its exit policy. `_note_bridge_refusal` moved to `auto_entry.note_bridge_refusal`; runner.py LINE_CAP 3391 -> 3365. - **Adaptive risk limits, lane B: wired in** (ADR 0031). The nightly `limits_job` (scheduler, daily 23:05 UTC, never caught up past the roll; `goldbot/ops/limits_job.py`) decides each demo account with ceilings for the next risk day. Inputs: the FULL history of its demo fills (net R after the ADR 0017 imputed cost) and of taken shadow trades of versions that went live, since each version's `promoted_utc`, cut off before the decision day. A window would reset Amendment A1's 60-trade exploration count. Plus the engine file's drawdown and stage and the 15m ATR from the store. It persists through `AdaptiveController`, sends a dq_event (dq_events, source `adaptive_limits`) when evidence is missing or stale, and sends the owner an FYI on every change (masked account, no buttons). Health check `limits_controller:<account>` FAILs when the last decision is over 26 h old. The engine reads the decision through ADR 0032's seam (`engine/limits_apply.py` `AdaptiveLimitsController`). It takes the decision only at the 00:00 UTC roll, only tightens within a day (restarts too: seeded from the day's `limits_changes`), and gives the floors when the decision is not today's or the drawdown is 4%. `clamp` keeps it within [default .. ceiling], and the 8% revert gives the defaults. Live and tiny-live keep the defaults. The supervisor takes a lower published adaptive combined cap. Records carry `min_lot_exception`. `scripts/replay_limits.py` replays the record read-only (validates, never tunes; log each run in ADR 0031). Behaviour change: icm-demo now trades the floors (2% / 5%, minimum-lot cap 1.0% from the A1 exploration budget while the ATR rule allows) until the rules earn a loosening; `risk.adaptive_limits: false` restores ADR 0032's static ceilings. Gap: no 20-day cost/model series exists, so the cost rule is inert (BACKLOG 90).
- **Adaptive risk limits, lane A** (ADR 0031 with Amendment A1, rules frozen before any replay): `goldbot/risk/adaptive.py` computes the account daily/weekly caps, the supervisor caps and the minimum-lot cap from demo fills after each strategy's freeze. The statistic is a daily-R-sum LCB, and q is quarter-Kelly per strategy, the smaller of the trade and day terms, minimum over strategies. Loosening is demo-only, one step at the risk-day roll after 3 qualifying days and 10 new demo trades, never within 5 days of a tighten. Tightening is immediate (DD 4%, 4 losses at -0.8R, cost/model, size-down stage, weak statistic, shadow included). The demo minimum-lot cap starts with an exploration budget: 1.0% for the first 60 exception trades, off for good at -10R cumulative, paused by ATR, stage, cost, DD and the loss streak; then the LCB rule decides. Live accounts stay at the defaults; anything missing or corrupt gives the floors and a dq_event. State and an append-only change log live in core.db migration 4 (`adaptive_state`, `adaptive_changes`), after ADR 0032's migration 3. Not wired yet: lane B adapts it to ADR 0032's `LimitsController` seam.

- Account type no longer blocks entries for a week: `nightly_costs` re-runs the classifier every night while the stored
  class is unknown (missing file or "unknown"; `PersistentClassifier.is_known`) and on Fridays only once a class is
  known (evidence thresholds and the two-disagreement rule unchanged). New optional `account_class: raw|standard` per
  account in `config/accounts.yaml` (set for icm-demo only) is the baseline until a measured class is stored;
  `execution/classifier.effective_class` is the one function the engine, smoke and state use; effective = the stricter of declared and the last
  KNOWN measurement (a stored unknown falls back to `last_known`; an unreadable classifier file with a declared class
  is standard); a disagreeing
  measurement makes the stricter class (standard) win and the engine health check warns "declared raw, measured
  standard: check the account type". Entry status: "only N London/NY ticks" is a self-clearing wait ("N of 1,000
  market ticks recorded; checked every night"), a declared class with no measurement is an info note, every other
  unknown reason still "Needs you". RiskGate logic and thresholds unchanged; unknown still blocks. The engine state
  gained `account_class_declared` and `account_class_measured` (golden hashes regenerated).
  A torn classifier file is recorded as `classifier_error` in the nightly row; the other accounts and the costs publish go on.

  small-account-playbook-2026-10-18 section 3: research no longer claims £ from trades the account cannot take.

  `run_specialist`/`evaluate`/`run_pool(..., lot_fit=LotFitSpec)` add `metrics.lot_fit` (model_filtered and

- Parallel research trials, serialized registry record (`research.yml`, `goldbot/research/cells.py`). The workflow is now
  `plan` -> `trials` (matrix, `max-parallel: 10`, `contents: read` only) -> `record` (`concurrency: research-registry`,
  the only job that writes the registry or an issue). Inputs: the existing single-trial ones (one cell per variant, so
  `variants` now runs in parallel) and a new `batch` (JSON list of `{specialist, variants, pooled, timeframe, ...}`, a
  missing key takes the dispatch input; max 64 cells). Each cell fetches bars and a read-only registry snapshot, runs
  `research_pass.py` on a copy of it and uploads only the rows it added. `record` fetches the fresh registry under the
  lock, merges the rows (registry_sync's keyed union, idempotent on a re-run), restates every deflated Sharpe and the
  gate's DSR verdict on the FINAL `n_trials_effective` (`cells.restate_dsr`; the run's own value stays in
  `results.dsr_at_run`), saves by the usual compare-and-swap and posts one comment per `research: <family>` issue.
  - A cell's own report is provisional: its DSR and trial numbers use the snapshot count, not its siblings; the posted
    report says so and shows `at run -> restated on K`.
  - A cell that crashed, timed out or left no artifact records a `failed` trial row (counted in N, never passes a gate).
    A cell refused before any look (budget, queue, holdout rule; a message, no traceback) records nothing and is listed.
  - Known limit: each cell checks the quarter's budget on its snapshot, so a batch can overshoot it by up to its size;
    the report states the quarter's count after the record. Size a batch to the remaining budget.

- TradingView lane A (plots -> point-in-time features, plan docs/plans/tradingview-strategies.md): `goldbot/data/tv_catalog.py` reads a study's `metaInfo` (`StudyMeta.from_metainfo`, unknown timeframe refused) and catalogues every readable plot with no owner naming: kind from the plot type and a 5 % level band, side only from an event's title (unknown = feature only, never a trigger), feature id `tv_{study}_{meta_hash8}_{tf}_{plot_id}` (an input or version change is a new id). `goldbot/features/tv_plots.py` registers `tv_plots` v1 on `enable()` (opt-in): ctx `tv_catalog` + `tv_indicators`, only rows of the study's own `meta_hash`, asof_join on `available_utc` with history available no earlier than bar close + 60 s (same as live, so training and live agree at the bar open), NaN when the bar is missing, late or blanked (1 % seeded with ctx `tv_training`), live rows (alert, `pull_live`) always, history (`csv`, `pull_history`) only when repaint-validated. `MetaLabelModel.fit` refuses more than 8 `tv_` columns (`check_feature_cap`). `tv-repaint-check --origin pull_history --meta-hash H` validates one input set of pulled history against live rows only; `meta_hash` is now part of the `tv_indicators` store key. The older `tradingview` feature reads `pull_history` as history and keeps versions and input sets apart. Not done: the pull writer, wiring into a research run.
- TradingView webhook: the shared secret is checked before schema validation (one uniform 403 for any unauthenticated body, no schema oracle), and the SQLite inbox takes at most `webhook.max_rows_per_hour` (default 5000) rows an hour, then 429 (logged without the body).
- An approval whose send raises is archived NOT CONFIRMED, never left placing (BACKLOG 84, implementer, 2026-10-17;
  trading-safety residual on BACKLOG 72).
  - `ApprovalCenter._finish`: if `on_decision` raises, the card's `placing` flag is cleared and it is archived with
    the refusal code `not_confirmed` and the facts pending (as `unconfirmed.archive_pending` does), then the error is
    re-raised. A refusal or NOT CONFIRMED the engine already archived stands. The outbox reports it NOT CONFIRMED
    at once instead of after PLACING_MAX_S, and the dashboard no longer shows "submitted" and then drops it.
  - `engine/unconfirmed.py`: a `sending` row (the send raised, or the engine died mid-send and the outbox's
    silent-engine fallback reported the card NOT CONFIRMED) whose position is found later, by `_resolve_sent`
    (restart or stale-sending) or by the reconcile adopt, sends the "opened" notice once and rewrites the card.
    `_card` also rewrites a card still `placing` (`shown_unconfirmed`), which sets `not_confirmed`, the refusal code
    and clears `placing`. A `sending` row with no card shown NOT CONFIRMED (the auto path) is adopted silently, as
    before. No new owner-facing strings and no runner change.
  - Not covered: an engine silent for 60 s whose send then returns a plain fill (status `filled`, no look-up). The
    outbox has already reported NOT CONFIRMED, and no "opened" notice follows. A raise before the order row exists
    (for example `last_tick`) is also archived NOT CONFIRMED with nothing to look up, so the dashboard lists it as
    pending until UNCONFIRMED_LISTED_S. Both are routed to trading-safety.
- An approval that raises before its order row exists is archived "not sent", never "approved and sent" or NOT
  CONFIRMED (BACKLOG 85, implementer, 2026-10-17; trading-safety residual 1 on BACKLOG 84).
  - `Engine._on_decision` now wraps the old body (`_apply_decision`); on any raise it calls
    `unconfirmed.archive_not_sent`, then re-raises. With no `pending_orders` row for the proposal (nothing can have
    reached the broker) and no answer archived yet, the card gets the refusal code `not_sent:mt5_box` (a bridge error
    or a connection failure, e.g. `account()` at approval) or `not_sent:engine` (anything else), `placing` cleared,
    archived, one owner notice and a `not_sent` journal row. A raise after the row exists keeps BACKLOG 84 (NOT
    CONFIRMED, entries refused until the look-up settles it). No row, so nothing is pending and the next entry is
    allowed.
  - Wording in `goldbot/execution/not_placed.py` (`not_sent_code`, `NotPlaced.not_sent`, `by` gains "engine"): card
    "🛑 NOT PLACED: approved, but the order could not be sent: the MT5 box couldn't be reached. Nothing was sent.";
    dashboard red "Could not be sent. …; nothing was sent."; the notice names the trade and the masked account, never
    the proposal id, the exception, a host or a login. Rows added to docs/ux/order-not-placed.md for ui-ux approval.
  - API contract: `NotPlaced.by` gains "engine" and `NotPlaced.not_sent` (bool) is added; web/openapi.json and
    web/src/lib/schema.d.ts regenerated, `ProposalCard` picks the "Could not be sent" heading.
  - Trading-safety review LOW: only `BridgeError`, `ConnectionError` and `TimeoutError` read "the MT5 box couldn't be
    reached"; any other `OSError` (a local disk or file error) is `not_sent:engine`. The digest and the performance
    report count a not-sent card under "not placed by the MT5 box, the broker or the engine" (`CAUSE_PHRASE`).
- Broker tick record for the H-A holiday diagnostic (BACKLOG 79, data-engineer, 2026-10-17).
  - New daily scheduler job `tick_record`. For each enabled account it pulls the broker's XAUUSD ticks of closed
    server dates with `copy_ticks`, read-only, through the scheduler's existing broker connection (`_job_broker`,
    the one feed_reconcile and broker_ledger use). Each day goes to `state/ticks/<account>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.parquet`.
  - Trading-safety review (bridge load), fixed:
    - Two slots, 21:10 and 22:10 UTC, one in each DST regime's daily break, each with `max_late_hours` 0.5.
    - The job skips unless `market_quiet` holds (New York 17:05-17:50, or the weekend), and stops when the window
      ends.
    - Pages of 2000 rows with a 0.2 s pause. A page over 2 s or a run over 300 s stops the run; the unfinished day
      is not written.
    - One day per run, oldest first; the weekend runs catch up.
    - A test proves the job is read-only: its fake broker's order methods raise.
  - File contents: `time_ns` (int64, through `epoch_ns`), `bid`, `ask`, `flags`. Written atomically, mode 0600, in
    a 0700 directory. `index.json` records rows, London/NY ticks, median spread, bytes and sha256 per day.
  - Re-runs are idempotent. Missed days within `ticks.backfill_days` (7) are back-filled. Days older than
    `ticks.retain_days` are pruned.
  - Health `ticks:<account>` (WARN only) when the newest day has fewer than `ticks.min_london_ny_ticks` (1000)
    London/NY ticks, or has not advanced in 4 days.
  - Loader: `goldbot.data.ticks.load_day(account, day, state_dir=...)`, which verifies the sha256.
  - Size: about 12 B/tick, so 50k ticks is about 0.6 MB a day.
  - Backup: the files are backed up (the whole state dir is). The terminal's tick history is finite, so a lost day
    cannot be pulled again.
  - Deviation from the lane brief: no recorder in the engine and no change to runner.py.
    - The engine already stores its polled `last_tick` sample in `data/ticks/source=<account>`.
    - A polled sample misses ticks between reads, so it biases H-A's ticks-per-minute.
    - The pre-registration (docs/research/holiday-list-measurement-2026-10.md) fixes "copy_ticks after each server
      day closes, one Parquet per server date".
  - `retain_days` defaults to 240, not 90: H-A reads the 2026-11-26 file after 2027-04-30.
  - Not done:
    - the 90% uptime rule (terminal connection history);
    - compaction of the engine's per-minute `data/ticks` part files (about 1,400 files a day, existing debt).

- **E-6 day-summed DSR coded and wired into the survivor verdict (BACKLOG 76, implementer, 2026-10-17; code review
  APPROVE, quant review round 2 pending; not pushed).** The discovery survivors' reading rule (pre-registration
  2027Q1 O-5/O-6: "the day-summed DSR is also >= 0.95") is now a coded check.
  - **The record.** `metrics.day_summed_dsr` sums net R per UTC entry day over days with a trade only (G days), with
    var(SR) = 1/G and the skew and kurtosis of the daily sums. The entry day is `pipeline.entry_utc`: `ts_utc` plus
    one bar, the real entry. Every walk-forward (not a discovery trial) stores it with the trial as
    `results.model_filtered.day_summed`. Beside it are the per-trade DSR of the same R series and both effective ts
    (`dsr_per_trade_r`, `t_per_trade_r`). Those two are **R basis, not the gate DSR**, which is on `ret`.
  - **The reading.** `gates.day_summed_check(row, rows)` reads, on `registry.n_trials_effective(rows)` (the phase
    gate's K, both discoveries' K_eff included), two things: the gate's DSR from `gates.current_dsr` (moved there from
    `ops/gates_phase.py`, which imports it) and the day-summed DSR. It passes only if both are >= 0.95, and fails
    closed without stored inputs or below 200 trading days.
  - **The verdict path.** A pre-registration with `rule_id` "O-5"/"O-6" (`registry.DAY_SUMMED_RULE_IDS`) puts its
    evaluated trial under `director.survivor_decisions` and `survivor_refusal`:
    - `record_verdict`: "continue" needs the gates and the reading passed; otherwise "stop", or "inconclusive" when
      the inputs are missing.
    - A holdout slot goes live, and `promotion_refusal` / `passed_gates` count the survivor's pass, only with the
      reading passed.
    - H-02's survivors, pre-registered under their own rule, are not read by it.
  - **Rule amendment.** The pre-registration's O-5/O-6 text records the stricter amendments dated 2026-10-17, before
    any H-14 outcome: the 200-day floor, the entry day and the gate DSR on `ret`. The program director notes them for
    the owner.
  - **Not changed.** `research_gates`, the phase gate's numbers, stored Q4 results and any frozen reading. Rows
    written before this have no `day_summed`.
  - **Tests.** `tests/test_day_summed_dsr.py` (22) and a compat case in `tests/test_persistence_compat.py`.

  before the tick, no symbol info or tick is a refused close 10021, no partial close of another symbol); the paper
  broker keeps a quote per symbol (`set_quote`) and lists only its symbol in `positions()`, every symbol in

  `_retry_closes` read `account_positions()` and close every symbol and magic; an unreadable account book closes the
  `positions()` fallback and never clears the flag; the flag clears only on a flat `account_positions()` read (one

  (trading-safety E1 APPROVE, LOW 1 and LOW 4): a 10021 close on another symbol backs off with the market-closed

  entry the MT5 box or the broker definitely refused no longer archives as APPROVED. The engine stores
  `bridge_stale_order` (10006 with the bridge's stale prefix, tested before the retcode) or `broker_refused:<retcode>`
  (any other `DEFINITE_REJECT_RETCODES`) in `gate_refusal`, and queues exactly one owner notice per refusal. The
  paper broker's duplicate is `broker_refused:10027:paper`, worded "it was already sent; this repeat was refused" and
  never "Nothing was sent" (its first send went out; `NotPlaced.nothing_sent` false). One wording table,
  `goldbot/execution/not_placed.py`, feeds the Telegram card (`outcome_text`), the notice and the new API field
  `DecidedProposal.not_placed {by, reason, code, next_step, nothing_sent}`; the dashboard's red note reads it, with
  "Refused by the broker (code N); nothing was sent." for older APIs, and the card's state name is now "not placed".
  Ceiling codes keep their shipped words. A fill, any `ok` result or an ambiguous result (10008, 10010, 10012, -1,
  ...) still reads APPROVED. Not in this change: the amber "NOT CONFIRMED" state and auto-mode notices (open points
  in the spec, awaiting decisions).
- Order not confirmed (BACKLOG 72; plan `docs/proposals/2026-10-backlog72-not-confirmed-plan.md` with trading-safety
  conditions 1-7 and the PD/UX decisions; copy `docs/ux/order-not-confirmed.md`, byte for byte). An approved or
  automatic entry the broker neither filled nor definitely refused (10008, 10010, 10011, 10012, 10031, -1, any undefined
  code, `ok` without a position) no longer archives as ✅ APPROVED.
  - The pending_orders row becomes `ambiguous`. It stays in `sent_ids` and is never re-sent.
  - It is looked up at the broker on every pass: from `_reconcile`, before its adoption loop, and from `no_quote_pass`
    every `reconcile_every_s`, so it also runs with no ticks. The logic is in `goldbot/engine/unconfirmed.py`.
  - Outcomes:
    - a position is adopted with the stop sent, at the dealt lots. A missing or looser stop is put back in the same
      pass; a stop that can't be set tells the owner to set it in MT5;
    - an entry deal plus an exit deal found by position id (never by comment) is recorded as a closed trade, at the
      dealt lots;
    - `unfilled` only after two clean looks in this process at least 120 s apart;
    - otherwise it keeps looking: one "still not confirmed" notice and a health WARN at 600 s, and terminal `unknown`
      (with one notice) at 7 days, after which the row is pruned.
  - Entries are refused `unconfirmed_order_pending` while any row is unresolved (condition 1, refusal path). After
    review round 1, a `sending` row counts as unresolved: the engine is single-threaded, so a `sending` row seen at a
    gate check is a send that raised.
  - Notices: at most one per outcome, plus one correction if a fill turns up after "no trade". `SentOrder.notified` and
    `SentOrder.unknown_notified` are persisted before each notice is sent.
  - One wording table, `goldbot/execution/not_confirmed.py`, feeds `outcome_text`, the notices, the health line and the
    new API field `DecidedProposal.not_confirmed {outcome, heading, text, tone}`. A new `DecidedProposal.refusal_text`
    words the RiskGate codes on "Refused at approval".

    - Race (HIGH): `_finish` archives an approval as `placing` (new `Proposal.placing`) and clears it once the engine's
      `on_decision` has the broker's answer. `Outbox.finished` waits while a card is `placing`. If the engine loop
      heartbeat is older than 60 s, or the card has been placing for 120 s, it reports NOT CONFIRMED, never ✅
      APPROVED. The API shows such a card as "submitted".
    - `sending` path (condition 3): `_resolve_sent` with no position marks the row `ambiguous`, never `filled` or
      `unfilled` on one look; the look-up then decides with the two-look rule.
    - Clean look (condition 2): a look is clean only when the last quote is valid and no older than
      `stale_tick_seconds`. No look in `no_quote_pass` is clean, so "no trade" is never declared while the market is
      closed or the feed is down. A restart's first look (before any quote) is not clean.
    - A look that raises is logged and waits. The other rows and the reconcile loop go on.
    - `_adopt` puts the trade in the open table before `adopted` saves the row and tells the owner.
    - A late-adopted trade keeps the tighter of the stop sent and the broker's stop.

- Telegram NOT CONFIRMED card edited at resolution (BACKLOG 87; copy `docs/ux/order-not-confirmed.md`). This closes
  the "Not done" of BACKLOG 72.
  - When the outbox reports a card NOT CONFIRMED, the Telegram service keeps the ids of the reply messages that went
    out. They live in aux.db table `outbox_watch` (migration 9, additive).
  - On each poll it re-reads the archived proposal, which `engine.unconfirmed._card` rewrites at each resolution. When
    the outcome changes, it edits those replies to `not_confirmed.card_text` (OPENED, OPENED AND CLOSED, NOT PLACED,
    OPENED AFTER ALL, STILL NOT CONFIRMED). The shown outcome is recorded in aux.db, so a restart never repeats an
    edit.
  - Failed edits (review round 1): an edit Telegram refuses for good (`BadRequest`: already shown, deleted, too old;
    `Forbidden`) is not retried (`bot.edit_is_final`). A rate limit, timeout or network error keeps the card watched
    and is retried after 2 s, doubling to 300 s, for 10 attempts per outcome (about 13 minutes); then it is given up
    for that outcome and logged. The attempt count is kept in aux.db, so it survives a restart.
  - Known window: `finished` deletes the sent row before the service sends the NOT CONFIRMED reply, and the reply ids
    are recorded only after it went out. A crash between the send and `watch` (one aux.db write) leaves that card
    unedited at resolution. The reply ids can't be recorded earlier because they don't exist yet; the notice and the
    dashboard still carry the outcome.
  - The watch ends on a settled outcome (`not_confirmed.SETTLED`: opened, opened and closed, opened after all). "No
    trade" stays watched for the correction. The watch also ends when the archive is gone or after 8 days
    (`WATCH_MAX_S`).
  - A card whose reply never went out is never watched or edited. Every step is best effort and logged; a failed edit
    or a busy aux.db never stops the owner's notices in the same pass.
  - The edited message is the NOT CONFIRMED reply (the message that carries the outcome line), not the proposal text
    above it, which the bot cannot rebuild. No new owner-facing strings.
  - `TelegramBot._pump`'s outbox work moved into `_outbox_pass` so it can be tested without the network.
  - Engine path unchanged (no edit to `goldbot/engine` or `approvals._on_decision`).
  - Reviews needed: ui-ux, code.

- E-2 top-tercile cut (BACKLOG 75, implementer, 2026-10-17; plan docs/proposals/2026-10-backlog75-tercile-cut-plan.md
  with the quant plan review's conditions 1-7; TRACEABILITY M48). O-4 can now pre-register
  `DiscoveryConfig.threshold_rule: tercile_inner`.
  - The cut (`pipeline.fold_cuts`) is the 2/3 quantile (`method="linear"`) of the raw out-of-fold p. It uses only
    rows that are test rows of an earlier fold and also in fold k's `train_idx`. Only finite p count, and a fold
    with fewer than 50 such rows takes no trade. A candidate is taken when its raw p >= the cut, with no break-even
    floor. Overlapping test folds raise.
  - CPCV (`cpcv.path_selection`) takes the cut from p_raw before the 0.5 fill. Earlier groups on the path are the
    prior set, with no purged variant (quant ruling 1).
  - Default unchanged: `break_even_margin` gives byte-identical walk-forward and CPCV outputs (golden
    `tests/data/tercile_default_golden.json`, captured on 65ece6e before the change). It also keeps the same
    `reading_rule` string and the same `DiscoveryConfig` dump and config hash, because the default rule is left out
    of the dump, so H-02's pin and every queued hash hold.
  - Under the tercile rule the reading rule's "(cross-fitted, break-even + margin)" is replaced, and one sentence is
    added: "promotion needs a separate trial under the live rule".
  - The discovery row records `threshold_rule`, `tercile_q`, `tercile_method`, `margin`, `fold_cuts`, `retention` and
    `share_taken_below_breakeven`. The pre-registration plan records the rule pins.
  - A run under the other rule hashes differently, so it is a new trial. Against a pending queued row it is refused
    (`director.queued_mismatch`).
  - The pre-registration is amended (2026-10-17, before any H-14 count): the cut is pinned, O-4 names
    `tercile_inner`, and O-5/O-6 name the live rule.
  - Not changed: RiskGate, execution, live thresholds, Q4 rows, frozen readings.
  - Quant review round 1 (code APPROVE, quant REQUEST CHANGES), fixed in one commit:
    - Under the tercile rule, "continue" needs at least 1,000 taken trades (`reading_verdict(min_taken=)`, as O-4's
      rule reads). The clause says "(at least 1,000 taken)". The default rule and its string do not move.
    - `tercile_q` and `tercile_method` are `DiscoveryConfig` fields. They are in the dump and the config hash under
      the tercile rule, so another q is another trial, and the clause is built from them. Under the break-even rule
      all three are dropped from the dump, keyed on the literal "break_even_margin", and a non-default q is refused.
    - `check_threshold_config` refuses a tercile run with `step_months < test_months` (overlapping test folds). It
      runs in `discovery_pass` and in the pre-registration writer, before the budget check or any registry row.
    - `threshold_plan` also adds its four keys to default-rule pre-registration plans. Plans are not hashed, so this
      is harmless.

    `timeframe=None` with the threshold rule. TRACEABILITY row renumbered M47 to M48. Non-blocking quant item done:
    `cpcv.path_selection` / `run_cpcv` take the trial's `tercile_q`, not a fixed 2/3.
- The approval window no longer trusts the wall clock alone (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 60; needs trading-safety review).
  `Proposal.expired` was `time.time() > created + window_s`, so a backward clock step stretched the owner's 90 s
  window and a pending file stamped in the future (a restored backup, a bad write) stayed approvable. Now
  `window_over` (goldbot/telegram/approvals.py) uses the heartbeat rule of BACKLOG 58: a `created` more than
  `CLOCK_AHEAD_TOLERANCE_S` (5 s) ahead, or not a finite number, counts as expired. The bus, the outbox, the dashboard
  list and the digest all use it. The digest counts such a pending proposal as EXPIRED_UNAPPROVED. The engine's
  `ApprovalCenter` also keeps a monotonic deadline per proposal it raised, set at `propose` to now + `window_s`. A
  click after that deadline counts as EXPIRED_UNAPPROVED whatever the wall clock says. The deadline is in memory only,
  with no new persisted field. After a restart the engine holds no proposal, so one left on disk is never executed,
  and it expires by the wall-clock rule with the guard. One stamped days ahead is archived at engine start. Tests:
  tests/test_approval_window_clock.py.
- Attribution results verdicts follow ADR 0022 (2026-10-16, quant review of the results verdicts). The rule was
  recorded before the code, in its own commit. Changes in `goldbot/research/attribution.py`:
  - **Day-clustered errors.** t, `ci95_net` and the new `ci_adj` use standard errors clustered by entry UTC day
    (CR1, `epoch_ns`). Tripling a day's trades no longer raises t.
  - **Row bar.** Every cell carries `t_bar`, `ci_adj` and `verdict_adj`.
    - Breakdown rows use the Bonferroni bar `t_bar = max(2, Φ⁻¹(1 − 0.025/m))`, m = breakdown cells at the minimum,
      read on the row's days − 1 degrees of freedom. The report carries `t_bar` and `m`.
    - The overall cell, the challengers and the live fills use `max(2.0, t⁻¹_{G−1}(0.975))` (F4).
    - `verdict_adj` is signed if and only if `ci_adj` excludes 0.
    - A clustered se of exactly 0 while the trades disperse is "no se": indistinguishable, never a point range (B1).
    - The raw `verdict` (|t| >= 2) is kept for `read_attribution`.
  - **Telegram digest** (`goldbot/telegram/digest.py`, quant ruling F3): names only rows whose `verdict_adj` is
    signed, else "no row clears the bar (|t| ≥ t_bar over m rows) · overall ...".
  - **Live fills** are compared with the backtest's slippage prior, not with the measured table built from the same
    fills. `LiveFills.mean_table_usd` is now `prior_usd`.
  - **Stale note fixed.** The note on live realised R now points at `ClosedTrade.r` in `closed_trades*.jsonl`.

  **Change to the review's formula, ruled correct by the quant reviewer (2026-10-16).** The review's formula (CR0,
  normal quantile) fails the review's own family-wise test: 0.085 in theory, 0.072 over seeds 0–499, against a bar of
  0.07. CR1 with t on G − 1 degrees of freedom gives 0.049. The gates and the stop rule are unchanged.

  Tests: tests/test_attribution.py

  - ::test_zero_clustered_se_with_dispersion_is_not_evidence
  - ::test_overall_bar_is_two_or_the_t_quantile_on_days_minus_one_for_overall_challengers_and_live
  - ::test_cell_stats_duplicated_same_day_trades_do_not_raise_t
  - ::test_adjusted_verdict_is_signed_exactly_when_the_adjusted_interval_excludes_zero
  - ::test_live_fills_are_compared_with_the_backtest_slippage_prior_not_the_table_built_from_them
  - ::test_build_report_notes_do_not_say_live_r_unrecorded

- Account classifier: a stored Unknown no longer sticks (implementer, 2026-10-16, SRE review finding;
  trading-safety Low and Option B applied). `PersistentClassifier.update` (goldbot/execution/classifier.py) lets a
  stored "unknown" adopt a known class on its first run when that cannot relax the account: the class is Standard,
  or Raw was proven by commission, or `state["last_known"]` is Raw or None. Otherwise (last stored Standard, now a
  spread-only Raw) the two-run rule applies. `last_known` is the last raw/standard class actually stored as the
  class (never a pending run) and never expires. Legacy state files without it are migrated on load: a known
  stored class is used as-is; a stored unknown with any standard in the kept runs reads Standard; otherwise None.
  Before, a thin first run (< 1,000 London/NY ticks) stored "unknown" and a known class then needed two agreeing
  Fridays, so the demo account would have stayed blocked by `account_class_unknown` until Fri 30 Oct instead of
  23 Oct. Unchanged: Raw <-> Standard still needs two agreeing runs, and a known class falls back to Unknown only
  after two Unknown runs in a row. Entry-rule change: reviewed by `trading-safety-reviewer`. Tests in
  tests/test_risk_exec_webhook.py:
  ::test_a_stored_unknown_is_replaced_by_the_first_known_class_on_its_first_run,
  ::test_a_stored_unknown_adopts_standard_on_its_first_run,
  ::test_after_falling_from_standard_to_unknown_a_spread_only_raw_run_needs_a_second_agreeing_run,
  ::test_after_falling_from_standard_to_unknown_a_commission_raw_run_is_adopted_at_once,
  ::test_raw_runs_that_were_only_pending_never_count_as_the_last_known_class,
  ::test_a_last_known_standard_does_not_expire_after_more_than_twenty_unknown_runs,
  ::test_a_legacy_state_file_without_last_known_is_migrated_from_its_class_and_runs,
  ::test_a_known_class_needs_two_agreeing_runs_to_change_to_another_known_class,
  ::test_a_known_class_does_not_fall_back_to_unknown_on_one_thin_week.
- **Engine state keeps moving while the market is closed (2026-10-16; BACKLOG 59; trading-safety and SRE review
  pending).** The engine wrote `engine_<acct>.json` on tick time only. With the market closed the tick stamp is
  frozen, so the file stopped, and health failed `bridge_compat:<acct>` once its `checked_at` was 5 min old: a
  Telegram FAIL and a Healthchecks.io `/fail` every 2 min all weekend, and a FAIL/recovered pair every weekday evening.
  - **The fix.** On the live clock, and only while the session table has the market closed, the engine also writes
    its state when `state_every_s` (10 s) of host time has passed with no write (`Engine._state_heartbeat_due`,
    `_write_heartbeat` in `goldbot/engine/runner.py`). Any write restarts that timer, so the rate stays one per 10 s,
    with the same fsync rules. A host clock stepped back rewrites the file at once in any session (BACKLOG 58: no
    stamp from the future). A session table that cannot be read never takes the heartbeat. Replays and backtests
    (tick clock) are unchanged.
  - **Review HIGH, fixed.** The first version also wrote in market hours, so a quote frozen in an OPEN session kept
    `bridge_compat` OK and `engine` at WARN forever. Now the file ages in market hours as before: `bridge_compat`
    FAILs after 5 min and `engine` after 45 min (`test_a_frozen_feed_in_market_hours_is_never_masked_and_fails_health`).
  - **What the heartbeat does not do.** It reads no account and runs no stage machine, kill switch, weekend rule or
    other exit step. Those stay on the tick-time refresh, as before. It changes no EngineState field, so the gate sees
    exactly what it saw before. No change to the order or exit path; RiskGate untouched.
  - **Fields stay true.** The heartbeat restates `last_tick_age_s`, `tick_ahead_s` and `market_closed` on the host
    clock. On a weekend the file says the last tick is hours old and the market is closed. Before, it kept the last
    market-hours reading. Owner-visible: on a weekend the dashboard's entry status reads the engine's live state, not
    the "engine idle while closed" fallback. It shows only "Market closed": `stale_data` is skipped when the engine
    says the market is closed (`goldbot/api/entry_status.py`), so a weekend never reads like a fault.
  - **The age rules still bite.** Health's rules are unchanged. An engine that writes nothing still FAILs
    `bridge_compat` on the weekend (5 min) and `engine` 45 min after the reopen; `engine_loop` is unchanged.
  - **Backups, checked, left alone.** With no restic keys, `job:backup` and `job:restore_drill` FAIL, which is
    correct until the owner sets the keys; the reason names `goldbot accounts set <key>`. The job check's
    160-character cut (which drops "RUNBOOK 'Backups')") is handled in a separate lane.

- **Day anchors pinned (2026-10-16; BACKLOG 57, TRACEABILITY R40; trading-safety review pending).** No code reads
  `risk_day_anchor` or `feature_day_anchor`; the loss caps reset at 00:00 UTC (`timeutil.risk_day` and the four other
  places listed under "Finding: risk_day_anchor" below) and daily bars close at 13:30 New York (`timeutil.feature_day`).
  The settings are now pinned, not wired: `Settings._day_anchor_is_the_fixed_day` (goldbot/config.py) refuses any
  `risk_day_anchor` other than UTC 00:00 and any `feature_day_anchor` other than America/New_York 13:30 at load, with
  an error that names the fixed day and says to delete the key from `config/settings.local.yaml` (exact text in
  docs/RUNBOOK.md, "Settings refuse to load: a day anchor"). The comparison is exact, so `Etc/UTC` is refused too.
  - **Not changed.** When any cap resets: `tests/test_config.py::test_the_risk_day_and_so_the_loss_cap_reset_is_pinned_at_00_utc`
    pins `new_day` (no reset at 23:59:59.999 UTC, a reset at 00:00). The shipped yaml loads unchanged. Rollback-safe:
    an older release accepts any anchor and ignores it, as before.
  - **Deploy precondition (servers).** A server whose `config/settings.local.yaml` sets either key would stop loading
    its settings after this deploy. No server exists yet, so the precondition holds trivially for the first deploy.
    Any server set up later, before it takes a release with this change, must be checked:
    `grep -nE 'risk_day_anchor|feature_day_anchor' config/settings.local.yaml` must print nothing.
  - **Still an owner decision.** Moving the risk day itself (for example to the 22:00 UTC roll) needs one shared
    risk-day function for all five places, a migration for the persisted reset time and a trading-safety review.
- **The digest's "Yesterday" is the opportunity day (2026-10-16; BACKLOG 56, TRACEABILITY V10; code and ui-ux review
  pending).** Before this, the digest's proposals and trades lines covered the UTC calendar day, 00:00-24:00, while
  its month line used the opportunity day. A close at 23:00 UTC was in yesterday's trades and in today's month total.
  Both now use `goldbot/ops/report_days.py`: `day_before(now)` names yesterday and `day_bounds(day)` gives its
  [D-1 22:00, D 22:00) UTC instants. The digest does no day arithmetic of its own, and the month line is built from
  the same day.
  - **What the owner sees.** The header changes from "Yesterday (Thu 15 Oct, 00:00-24:00 UTC)" to
    "Thu 15 Oct trading day (ended 22:00 UTC, 23:00 UK)". The local time comes from `telegram.owner_tz` (default
    Europe/London, shown as "UK"; another zone shows its abbreviation) and is left out only if the zone cannot be
    resolved. With closes at Wed 22:30, Thu 10:00 and Thu 23:00 UTC, the Friday digest
    used to show "Closed 2 trades: net +$30.00 · +0.60R (1 won, 1 lost)" next to "October so far: ... 2 trades ·
    +1.50R". It now shows "Closed 2 trades: net +$80.00 · +1.50R (2 won, 0 lost)", the same trades as the month line.
    The Thu 23:00 close moves to Saturday's digest.
  - **Weekends.** Friday's opportunity day ends at 22:00 UTC, at or after the Friday close in both US DST regimes, so
    Saturday's digest reports Friday. Sunday's day, Sat 22:00 to Sun 22:00 UTC, holds no session: the reopen (22:00
    UTC in summer, 23:00 in winter) opens Monday's day. So Monday's digest says "Trades closed: none" for Sunday, and
    the reopen's closes arrive on Tuesday. Nothing is counted twice or dropped, and Friday is not repeated on Monday.
    A Saturday or Sunday with no proposal and no close shows one line instead of the two "none" lines: "Weekend:
    market closed, no trading. Sunday-evening trades show in Tuesday's digest." A weekend day that has rows (a winter
    Friday close stamped exactly 22:00 UTC is Saturday's) shows them as usual.
  - **Late sends (code review).** "Yesterday" is worked out from the scheduled slot (`DigestSchedule.slot`, passed
    by the bot as `build_digest(as_of=...)`), not from the send time. With `digest_at` 18:00, a send 4.5 h late at
    22:30 used to report the day just ended and the next day's digest reported it again, losing the day before. The
    first line and the expiry of pending proposals still use the send time. The month line now gets the day itself
    (`build_monthly_report(day=...)`). Tested in a summer week, the week US
    DST ends (1 Nov 2026) and a winter week.
  - **Not changed.** The risk line (drawdown, day and week loss against the caps) reads the engine's figures, which
    reset on the 00:00 UTC risk day. No limit, RiskGate check or engine code was touched. The digest has no day input
    to the risk line, so no digest test can catch it moving; the reset itself is pinned by
    `tests/test_report_days.py::test_the_risk_day_still_resets_the_day_start_equity_at_00_utc_not_at_the_22_utc_roll`.
  - Also: `goldbot/research/min_lot.py` `--size-down` help said "8% stage", which argparse read as a "% s" format and
    printed the action's attribute dict; now "8%%", with a test that `--help` renders.
  - Tests: tests/test_digest.py 10 new (12 cases), 1 updated; tests/test_report_days.py 2 new (5 cases);
    tests/test_min_lot.py 1 new. RUNBOOK 0.5 "Morning digest" updated.
- **The engine publishes why it refuses entries (BACKLOG 43, `entry_blocks` part; implementer).**
  `RiskGate.account_reasons(st, now)` is every account-level reason `check()` refuses for, and `check()` starts from
  it (one list, cannot drift). `engine_<account>.json` carries `entry_blocks` (those codes, at every state write; a
  heartbeat judges the feed it publishes) and `entry_refusals` (per agent, the last per-trade refusal and its time,
  cleared when the gate next allows that agent; in memory only). The API (`goldbot/api/entry_status.py`) now only
  words them: the flag mapping and the min-lot "Likely" fallback are gone, rollover and the weekend cut show, a
  strategy's last refusal is its own block "since" then, and an engine without `entry_blocks` shows
  `entry_reasons_missing` (act), never OPEN. Order change on refusals only: `account_class_unknown` and
  `open_risk_unknown` now come before the intent's own reasons. Deploy: brain and API together (same release);
  exits are never gated by any of it. R43; reviews owed: code-reviewer, trading-safety-reviewer (gate and engine),
  ui-ux-designer (new wording).

- Heartbeats stamped in the future fail closed (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 58). Before this, a `ts` ahead of the reader's
  clock, or a NaN, made `now - ts > limit` False, so a dead supervisor whose last write carried a fast clock (or came
  from a restored backup) never halted the engines. The shared rule is `goldbot.data.timeutil.heartbeat_problem`:
  a stamp that is not a finite number is `invalid`, one more than a tolerance ahead is `future`, one older than the
  limit is `stale`. Engines halt on `supervisor_heartbeat_future` (more than 5 s ahead, `CLOCK_AHEAD_TOLERANCE_S`)
  or `supervisor_state_unreadable` (a non-numeric or NaN `ts`, or a file that is not an object). The supervisor halts
  every entry on an engine file more than 5 s ahead (`engine_heartbeat_future`, files in `future_engines`; that
  file's currency and money still count). Health fails the supervisor, engine, engine loop, service heartbeat and
  scheduler lines (warns the alert loop) on a stamp more than the same 5 s ahead (`HEALTH_CLOCK_AHEAD_S`), measured
  against max(the pass's `now`, the wall clock) (`checks._base._ahead_s`, SRE review): a pass takes its `now` once
  and can run for minutes while the bridge times out, and a service that beat meanwhile is not a clock fault. The
  later clock can only clear a future flag, never raise one. The Feeds page shows such a supervisor heartbeat as not reporting, the
  dashboard hides combined caps read from it, and a bridge verdict confirmed in the future counts as `unchecked`.
  Left alone on purpose: report-age checks (drift, restore drill, ledger, crossfeed, costs, risk-day roll, re-arm,
  stuck approvals, job overdue), where a future stamp only hides a "report old" warning and the scheduler heartbeat
  still catches a dead producer; the bridge's order age (already refuses either way and on NaN); the tick checks
  (`tick_from_future`); in-process timers (watchdog, dead man's switch, runner timers).
- High-water-mark rises are confirmed (BACKLOG 54, ADR 0018, TRACEABILITY R40; needs trading-safety review). A
  balance read above `balance_closed_hwm` raises it only when the deal history since the mark was set explains it
  (closed deals, commission, swap, deposits; within `risk.hwm_rise_tolerance`, 0.1% of the mark), or when the next
  read agrees. Otherwise the mark stays where it is, the account is read again on the next tick, and the engine
  records `hwm_rise_unconfirmed`, then `hwm_raised` or `hwm_rise_refused`. One inflated balance read no longer
  causes a phantom size-down or kill switch later on. Deposits raise the mark, as before. The mark is never lowered
  (only /rearm resets it). The candidate and the deal-history anchor are stored in core.db (additive migration 2,
  table `hwm_confirmation`), not in a JSON file. A row taken for another mark is void. A restart keeps the candidate
  but never applies it unconfirmed. Health `risk:<account>` warns when a rise has waited more than 5 min in market
  hours, measured from the first of a run of disagreeing candidates. A rollback to an earlier release raises the mark
  on one read again. Review fixes (trading-safety review of faf824c):
  - a candidate that the deals after it carry to a later lower read was a real peak, and the mark rises to it;
  - candidates expire after 10 min;
  - core.db is opened once per engine, with a 500 ms write busy timeout;
  - the paper broker declares its balance reads exact, so one read raises the mark there.
  The ADR is renumbered 0018 (0017 is CostImputer).
- Integration chores scripted (implementer, 2026-10-16; throughput plan lever 4, TD-7, TD-8; ADR 0025 proposed,
  amends 0012). The work comes in four parts:
  - **Rendered-docs merge driver.** `.gitattributes` routes HANDOFF.md, TRACEABILITY.md and BACKLOG.md to the
    `goldbot-docs` driver. It re-renders each file from the fragments merged three-way, so a plain merge, rebase or
    cherry-pick no longer conflicts on them. A fragment edited on both sides, or two lanes taking one id, still
    stops the merge and names the fix.
    **Enable it once per clone:** `python scripts/docs_assemble.py install-merge-driver`.
  - **ADR numbers.** `docs_assemble.py new-adr --slug S --title T` reserves the next number under a lock in the git
    common dir, so parallel worktrees never share a number. It skips `docs/decisions/reserved.yaml`, which holds
    0023-0026 from the CTO register; `--number N` claims a reserved number. `check` fails on two ADRs with one number.
  - **Worktree prune.** `scripts/prune_worktrees.sh` is a dry run by default; `--apply` removes. It handles only
    merged, clean worktrees that have been idle for 24 h, and never the main checkout or a locked, dirty or unmerged
    tree. It also keeps a lane that never committed (a read-only reviewer) and one that holds ignored files outside
    the regenerable caches (an `.env`, say: `git worktree remove` would delete it silently).
  - **Lane dispatch checklist.** `docs/process/lane-checklist.md`.

  Tests: `tests/test_docs_assemble_chores.py`, `tests/test_prune_worktrees.py`.
- The kill switch's close-everything choice is now state (2026-10-16, trading-safety finding F1 MEDIUM; re-review
  APPROVED 6cf86e3, with two follow-ups fixed in the next commit). Before, `everything` was true only on the tripping
  read, and the owner-mode write (`ApprovalBus.set_mode`) ran before the flatten: in auto mode a full disk raised out
  of it and closed nothing, and a positions() read failing on that read did the same; every later run closed only this
  engine's magic range, so a manual or other-magic position stayed open. Now `Engine._kill_everything`
  (goldbot/engine/runner.py) is set before any I/O on the trip, saved with the risk state (`kill_everything` in
  `risk_<account>.json`; absent = false), used by every retry (tick, no-quote pass, halted refresh) and after a restart
  (`_kill_pending` starts true), and cleared only once a run has closed every XAUUSD position on the account (all
  magics; `MT5Broker.positions()` reads the engine's symbol only, so other symbols are untouched, an owner decision).
  The mode write moved after the flatten into `_reset_owner_mode`: it never raises, a failure is a tick error and is
  retried on the next kill-switch run, and a halted engine retries it after a restart (re-review LOW, A10); the
  in-memory `approval_mode = "propose"` already blocks auto entries. No stop widened, no size added, no new order path.
  ADR 0016 carries the correction. Tests: tests/test_kill_switch_everything.py (7).
- Lane test loop (2026-10-16): lanes iterate on affected tests only with `scripts/lane_test.sh` (pytest-testmon):
  `seed` copies the integrator's `.testmondata` for the lane's base commit from `~/tmp/testmon/<sha>/` (`cp -c`;
  without one the first `iter` runs the full suite), `iter` runs `pytest --testmon -n ${GATES_WORKERS:-2} -q` (never
  with `-m`: testmon turns selection off under `-m`), `final` reminds the lane to run `scripts/gates.sh` once before
  handing back. The integrator runs `refresh` on a clean checkout at the integration tip to (re)build and publish the
  DB for that sha. Rule: lanes iterate with `scripts/lane_test.sh iter`; the full suite (`scripts/gates.sh`) runs once
  before handing back; the integration branch and release run the full gates. Selection is iteration only and
  misses non-Python inputs (config, data files) that testmon does not track, which is why the full gates stay.
- `test_lockout_survives_a_restart` no longer depends on the wall clock (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 55). Root cause: the
  lockout counts `auth_failures` rows by `time.time_ns` and prunes rows older than 15 minutes on every attempt, so a
  run where the wall clock moved 15 minutes between the first failure and the restarted sign-in (a paused VM, a
  starved worker) pruned the five failures, and the sign-in went through ("DID NOT RAISE"). A lock held on aux.db
  past `busy_timeout` was ruled out: it raises `database is locked` and never lets a sign-in through. The test now
  takes the `lockout_clock` fixture (tests/conftest.py: `time.time_ns` pinned, moved only by the test) and restarts
  the store 1 s before the window ends. That makes it stronger: it now fails when the window is halved as well as
  when the failure write is disabled. Evidence: with the lockout clock running 10,000 times faster than real time
  (a scratch pytest plugin), the old test failed 20 of 20 and the new one passed 200 of 200; it also passed 200 of
  200 under CPU stress (load average up to 256). Production code is unchanged: `_reserve` checks and counts in one
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, and no race was found.
  - Follow-up for the test-engineer: the other lockout tests (tests/test_api.py `test_lockout_after_five_failures`,
    `test_one_ip_is_limited_across_many_emails`, tests/test_api_code_lockout.py) still use the wall clock and can
    fail the same way. They can switch to `lockout_clock`.

  counts as stale, as in `engine_should_halt`), dated ahead or without its caps, `account_view._combined` dropped the
  combined 1.5%/4% caps. The Overview card and the safety-strip chip then showed the engine's 2% daily cap, the
  roomier figure. Now:
  - `LossBudget.unknown` carries the owner's reason (for example "The safety supervisor hasn't reported for over a
    minute, so the combined loss cap can't be checked. New entries are paused; exits always run.").
  - `LossBudget.unknown_paused` says whether the engines pause new entries on the same report. When they do, the
    card ("Loss budget: can't check", the reason, no amount) and the chip ("can't check") are red. They are amber
    when the supervisor hasn't added up the accounts yet.
  - The approval cards read "loss budget left today: can't check (supervisor not reporting; new entries paused)" on
    Telegram, and the same in red on the web. `/api/proposals` gains `loss_cant_check` ("paused" / "not_summed"),
    with `loss_left` null.
  - A cap rebuilt from settings was rejected: one account's equity misses the other accounts' losses.
  - Entry blocks are unchanged: the account caps stay in `caps`, and the engines already halt on the report.
  - Mixed currencies still show the account cap (BACKLOG 61).

  Tests: `test_a_rejected_supervisor_report_shows_the_budget_as_unknown_never_the_roomier_account_cap` (API, five

  `test_a_rejected_or_capless_supervisor_report_means_the_budget_cant_be_checked_with_the_reason`, and the

- **One north-star day for the owner's reports (2026-10-16; TRACEABILITY V9, BACKLOG 57; quant and trading-safety
  review pending).** Before this, the monthly report used the UTC calendar day. The performance report used the
  opportunity day, which rolls at 22:00 UTC. Each had its own day-bucketing and weekday-count code, so a close between
  22:00 and 24:00 UTC landed on different days in the two reports. Both now use `goldbot/ops/report_days.py`
  (`report_day`, `weekdays`, `month_days`, `day_buckets`, `DAY_BOUNDARY`). The one definition of the day,
  `opportunity_day` with `ROLLOVER_UTC_H = 22`, moved from `features/day_type.py` to `goldbot/data/timeutil.py`, next
  to `risk_day`. `day_type` re-exports it, so the features, H-16 and their goldens are unchanged.
  - **The day.** Day D runs from D-1 22:00 UTC to D 22:00 UTC. That time is inside gold's 17:00-18:00 New York break
    in both US DST regimes, so the Sunday reopen counts on Monday and the Friday close on Friday. Tests pin this
    around 22:00 UTC and in the March and November DST weeks (including the US-EU gap week).
  - **Changes the owner will see in the monthly report and the digest's month line.**
    - A close between 22:00 and 24:00 UTC now counts on the next day. That moves best days and £50+ days.
    - The month follows the day too. A close at 23:30 UTC on the month's last day is in the next month's report.
    - The default month is the month of now's opportunity day. At 31 Oct 23:00 UTC that is November.
    - Trading days are the Monday-Friday opportunity days elapsed, today's included.
    - The digest's "month so far" (built at `now - 1 day`) now runs to yesterday's 22:00 UTC roll. A close after the
      roll waits for the next digest.
    - The report's second line now reads "days run from 22:00 UTC the evening before (the opportunity day; the Sunday
      reopen counts on Monday)". "(UTC)" is gone from the title line.
  - **Not changed.** pnl_basis: both reports pick their rows (net only, account currency only) before they bucket
    them, as they did before. The loss caps stay on the risk day (00:00 UTC). So does perf_report's drawdown against
    the limits (`risk_day`, `_risk_week`). No limit, RiskGate check or engine code was touched.
  - **Known gap (digest, not in this lane).** The digest's "Yesterday" line is still the UTC day, 00:00-24:00. A close
    at 23:00 UTC is in yesterday's trades line but in today's month line.
  - **Review follow-ups (quant and trading-safety approved).**
    - ADR 0004 section 6 now records both days: the north-star day is the opportunity day, and the £50 loss limit
      stays on the risk day. DESIGN.md "Time and calendar" now names the reports as users of the fourth day.
    - perf-report's default `--from` is now the first day of the month that holds today's opportunity day. At 31 Oct
      23:00 UTC the default range is 1 Nov to 1 Nov, the month the monthly report shows (`perf_report.default_range`).
    - Before the month's first weekday, the monthly report and the digest show the average per trading day as "n/a"
      (`avg_per_day` None), not £0.00. A winter Friday close at 22:00 UTC lands on the Saturday, for example.
    - The digest's "Yesterday" line is now BACKLOG 56. BACKLOG 57 now says to check each server's
      settings.local.yaml before the validator ships, and to put its error text in the RUNBOOK.
  - **Finding: `risk_day_anchor` is read by no code (for the quant and trading-safety reviewers).**
    - Where it is: `Settings.risk_day_anchor` (`goldbot/config.py:491`) and `config/settings.yaml:7`
      (`{ tz: UTC, time: "00:00" }  # loss caps reset`). No code under goldbot/ or scripts/ reads it, and
      `feature_day_anchor` is unread too (`resample.py` uses its own defaults).
    - Where the 00:00 UTC risk day is actually decided, each place on its own:
      - `timeutil.risk_day` (`goldbot/data/timeutil.py:163`), used by `gate.new_day` (`goldbot/risk/gate.py:537`),
        `throttle.entries_on_day` (`goldbot/risk/throttle.py:83`) and perf_report's drawdown;
      - the engine's own UTC `.date()` shortcut in `_roll_risk_period` (`goldbot/engine/runner.py:2129`);
      - the "resets" time on the entry-status card, `_next_day` (`goldbot/api/entry_status.py:235`);
      - `gate._risk_week`, Sunday 00:00 UTC (`goldbot/risk/gate.py:530`);
      - the supervisor follows the engines through their published `day_start_equity`
        (`goldbot/risk/supervisor.py:156`).
    - Risk today: an owner who sets `risk_day_anchor` in `settings.local.yaml` believes the caps' reset has moved, and
      nothing tells them it has not. If only `risk_day` honoured it, the reset would still happen at 00:00 UTC: the
      runner's `.date()` shortcut returns before `new_day` runs between the anchor and midnight. The card would also
      show the wrong "resets" time, and the perf report's drawdown would disagree with the gate.
    - **Recommendation.**
      1. Now (trading-safety review, BACKLOG 57): pin the setting. A Settings validator should refuse any value other
         than UTC 00:00 at load, saying the risk day is fixed. That only tightens, and it is safe on rollback (an older
         release ignores the key). `tests/test_report_days.py::test_the_configured_risk_day_anchor_is_the_hard_coded_risk_day`
         already pins the shipped yaml.
      2. Do not honour it piecemeal. Moving the risk day to the 22:00 UTC roll would stop one Asia session's losses
         being split across two caps at midnight. But it changes every daily-cap reset. It needs one shared
         risk-day function for all five places above, a migration for the persisted `_last_reset`, and an owner
         decision with a trading-safety review. Do it only if the quant reviewer finds the midnight split matters in
         measured trades.
    - A regression test pins today's behaviour: `new_day` does not reset at 22:30 UTC and does at 00:00.

    tests/test_currency_followups.py: `account_month` now takes its first and last opportunity days as YYYY-MM-DD.

- Round-trip costs in the daily £ projection (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 36, trading-safety review LOW-6). Accounts with
  an absolute daily loss limit (icm-demo, £50) now refuse an entry when loss so far (+ open risk) + stop risk + round
  trip > the limit. Before, the round trip was left out. The round trip has two parts, both x lots x contract x fx in
  the account currency:
  - spread, slippage and commission: `cost_atr` x ATR, the engine's `_cost_atr` (the nightly cost table, else
    `cost_atr: 0.10`);
  - the paid swap, when a broker rollover falls before 00:00 UTC.

  The swap reuses ADR 0017's rule. `cost_imputation.account_swap` takes the table's measured rates, else the settings
  prior. `paid_swap_per_oz` counts the triple day and never counts a credit. The closed-trade charge now calls the same
  two helpers. The projection can only grow: a negative cost or a credit counts as 0, and a NaN swap refuses
  (`invalid:swap_usd_per_oz`). The approval re-check prices the swap again at the click. No other check reads the
  cost, and exits are untouched. Worked example at £5,000 GBP (fx 0.75, ATR $10, 0.01 lot): stop £7.50, round trip
  £0.30, one night of the -$60 prior £0.45 (£1.35 on Wednesday). With £42 lost, the projection was £49.50 (allowed)
  and is now £50.25 (refused). New `GateDecision.cost_amount` and `Intent.swap_usd_per_oz` (in-memory only, nothing
  persisted). Tests: tests/test_projection_costs.py; three older boundary pins moved by exactly the cost.

  Trading-safety review fixes (one MEDIUM, four LOW):
  - A NaN swap rate no longer reads as "pays nothing". `SwapSpec` and the cost table's swap fields are finite-only,
    so a NaN table fails to load and the prior is charged. A NaN broker reading becomes "no swap" in the nightly job.
    If a non-finite rate still reaches the engine, `_swap_usd_per_oz` returns NaN and the gate refuses.
  - A swap that cannot be priced at the click refuses the approval (`swap_unavailable`).
  - The spread is counted twice on purpose: `cost_atr` includes it, and so does the stop risk measured from the fill.
    This is conservative and recorded in the gate comment and R42.
  - Quant, code and trading-safety reviews done.
- Quant review 2026-10-16 fixes (e501d56, 1589755, 4ed8270; quant-reviewer re-review owed, gate 1 is on the
  promotion path).
  - HIGH: gate 1 (`backtest_to_paper`) and gap watch read `registry.promotion_refusal` / `promotion_pass_counts`:
    `gate_pass_counts`, plus the latest evaluated rerun of the config decides, plus a `from_discovery` config needs
    its passed holdout scoring (the rule `passed_gates` already applied). A discovery-derived pass without its
    holdout no longer meets gate 1 or becomes the paper/live backtest reference.
  - MEDIUM: `metrics.summarize` stores `dsr_inputs` (`DsrInputs`: sr, n, skew, kurtosis, var_sr_trials). Gate 1
    recomputes the DSR on the registry's current `n_trials_effective`; a row without stored inputs fails the `dsr`
    item closed ("no stored DSR inputs ... re-run the trial"). Every registry row written before this commit is in
    that state, so gate 1 stays unmet until the best trial is re-run.
  - MEDIUM: `passed_gates` no longer takes best-of-N over reruns: only the latest evaluated row (same family, config
    hash, feature version, costs recorded) decides. Gap watch now founds from the latest rerun's trial id.
  - MEDIUM: the ruin Monte Carlo prices a closed trade without R from its stop, side x (exit - entry) / |entry -
    initial stop|, and charges it as a price return. A row that cannot be priced is left out, counted
    (`n_excluded`, in the report notes) and makes the cost basis "unknown".
  - LOW: `research_pass` refuses a matching pending queued row that pins no `data_digests`; `--discover` refuses to
    run when `research.holdout_from` is set but `holdout_window()` is None.
  - Tests: tests/test_phase_gates.py (gate_1_* tests), tests/test_research_discipline.py
    ::test_a_later_failing_rerun_of_the_same_config_revokes_an_earlier_pass, tests/test_gate_pass_counts.py,
    tests/test_ruin.py::test_a_price_return_row_without_r_is_priced_from_its_stop_and_charged_not_dropped,

- Trial registry push re-checks the release asset just before the swap (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 51). The VPS monthly loop
  pushes `research-v1/registry.jsonl` outside the workflows' `concurrency: research-registry`, so a workflow save
  that landed between the loop's pull and its push was overwritten, and the other way round too. Both writers now run
  one implementation: `goldbot.research.registry_sync`, over HTTP on the VPS and through `gh` in the workflows.
  `scripts/registry_release.sh fetch | save | recover` is a thin wrapper over it. Each save is a compare-and-swap:
  - Note the asset's stamp (id, updated_at, size, digest) at the pull.
  - Upload the merged rows as `registry.jsonl.pending-*`.
  - Re-read the stamp, then delete the pulled asset by its id.
  - Rename the pending asset, then re-read: published means our id is the lowest-id `registry.jsonl`, with the
    deleted id filtered out. The rename's status code is not relied on. A re-read that still lists the deleted id,
    or does not list our upload, is stale and is read again after a wait; our upload is never dropped on one.

  Downloads are by asset id (`gh api -H 'Accept: application/octet-stream' .../releases/assets/<id>`), and every
  `gh` call times out after 120 s. `recover` prints what each copy adds (row count and trial keys) before it
  publishes.

  Another writer is detected by a changed stamp, a 404 on the delete, or another copy being published at the rename.
  The pending upload is then dropped, and the writer waits a jittered 0.5-1.5 s per attempt, pulls, merges and
  retries, at most 3 times. After that it fails loudly. On the VPS, `registry_sync` records `failed: ...` and the
  loop carries on; in a workflow the job fails. The local file keeps every union it saw, so a lost race drops no
  row. The keyed union counts each trial once in the deflated Sharpe.

  Once the old asset is deleted, the pending upload is never deleted unless another copy is published. If the rename
  keeps failing, the upload stays and the save fails with "run `scripts/registry_release.sh recover`". `recover`
  unions every `registry.jsonl` and `registry.jsonl.pending-*` on the release and publishes the result the same way.
  Reads never start from an empty registry when the release exists, in two cases:
  - a pending upload with no published copy (a writer mid-swap, or stranded);
  - a release with no `registry.jsonl` at all, unless `--bootstrap` is passed.

  The refusal of a union shorter than the published copy is kept, and the VPS applies it too. `--clobber` is no
  longer used. GitHub has no conditional upload, so the re-check alone is not atomic with the delete; the delete by
  id and the post-rename re-read are what keep that window safe. A writer outside this protocol (a manual
  `gh release upload --clobber`) is still not protected against.

  Rollback: a pre-51 VPS release reads a pending-only release as an empty registry and its push deletes and
  re-uploads `registry.jsonl` directly. Do not roll the VPS back while a pending asset is stranded; run `recover`
  first.

  Tests: tests/test_registry_push_race.py and tests/test_registry_release.py. They cover another writer landing
  after the upload, before the delete and during the rename; a rename that fails, or answers 200 without renaming;
  two protocol writers interleaved, including the first-ever push; a failed re-check; recover; bootstrap; and the
  bounded-retry failure.
